common_notes: Limits are per angler; select the actual species and keep it identifiable. California fishing license required for anglers age 16 and older.

For finfish, the general daily limit is 20 total, with no more than ten of one species unless a specific exception applies; lower species and group limits still apply. Lingcod and RCG count toward 20. The reviewed bluefin and albacore allowances are additional-limit exceptions.
MPAs, local closures and the Diablo Canyon security zone override an area-wide open season. Check the exact fishing position in CDFW’s official map.
For finfish, carry a landing net with an opening of at least 18 in. South of Pigeon Point, within 1,000 yd of shore, metallic/wire lines or leaders and hooks wider than 1½ in inside are prohibited.
Proposals and staff recommendations are not current rules. Pending 2026 measurement amendments and MPA petitions do not change these limits until legally effective and reviewed.

lingcod.name: Lingcod
lingcod.season: Apr 1–Dec 31, 2026 · boat fishing at all depths in the Central Management Area.
lingcod.bag: 2 per person daily; 2 in possession. Separate from the 10-fish RCG limit.
details: Use one line with no more than two hooks when targeting lingcod, or when lingcod are aboard. Your double-drop rig fits that limit.
Carry a descending device ready for immediate use.
Fillets aboard: at least 14 in, with all skin attached.

rod.note: This profile is for recreational rod-and-reel fishing from a boat. Read the species-specific hook, line, retention and on-board restrictions below.

rockfish.name: Rockfish / rock cod
rockfish.season: Apr 1–Dec 31, 2026 · boat fishing at all depths in the Central Management Area.
rockfish.bag: 10 total rockfish, cabezon and greenlings combined per person daily and in possession.
rockfish.size: No minimum length for retained rockfish. Species must be identified.
details: Within the 10: at most 1 copper, 2 canary, and 2 vermilion/sunset rockfish combined.
No retention of yelloweye, quillback, cowcod or bronzespotted rockfish.
Use one line with no more than two hooks when targeting rockfish, or when rockfish are aboard. Carry a descending device ready for use.
Retained rockfish fillets must have all skin attached.

rod.note: This profile is for recreational rod-and-reel fishing from a boat. Read the species-specific hook, line, retention and on-board restrictions below.

halibut.name: California halibut
halibut.season: Year-round in the reviewed 2026 rules. This card covers waters south of Point Sur.
details: California halibut only; Pacific halibut has a different season and rules.
General ocean hook-and-line rules apply. With rockfish or lingcod aboard, use one line and no more than two hooks; salmon aboard triggers salmon gear rules.
Fillets aboard: at least 16¾ in with all skin attached. Do not gaff an undersized fish.
Do not halve halibut fillets. A lengthwise midline split is allowed only if the pieces remain joined for at least two inches at one end; retain all skin and the minimum fillet length.

rod.note: This profile is for recreational rod-and-reel fishing from a boat. Read the species-specific hook, line, retention and on-board restrictions below.

salmon.name: Chinook salmon
salmon.season: Closed for the remainder of 2026. 2027 ocean salmon season dates are set in March and April 2027.
salmon.bag: None: the recreational ocean salmon fishery is closed for the rest of 2026.
salmon.size: Not applicable while the fishery is closed.
details: CDFW Central Region page (updated Nov 7, 2026): the recreational ocean salmon fishery is closed for the remainder of the year. 2027 dates are not yet set; check CDFW before any 2027 trip.
North of Point Conception: one rod and no more than two single-point, single-shank barbless hooks when targeting salmon or with salmon aboard.
When using bait other than while trolling, use barbless circle hooks. Two hooks must be rigidly tied no more than 5 in apart.
Do not fillet salmon aboard before landing ashore.

rod.note: This profile is for recreational rod-and-reel fishing from a boat. Read the species-specific hook, line, retention and on-board restrictions below.

albacore.name: Albacore tuna
albacore.season: Year-round in the reviewed 2026 rules. Offshore U.S. waters north of Point Conception.
albacore.bag: 25 per person daily and in possession, in addition to the general 20-finfish limit.
albacore.size: No minimum size in these recreational rules.
details: The albacore limit drops to 10 south of Point Conception (34°27′ N). This card does not cover Mexico.
General ocean hook-and-line rules apply; fish already aboard can impose stricter rod and hook limits.
If processing tuna aboard south of Point Conception, follow the tuna-specific fillet, skin and bag-label requirements in §27.65. This card covers day trips; multi-day possession rules differ.
If any part of an albacore trip enters U.S. EEZ waters south of 34°27′ N, no more than 10 albacore per person may be onboard for that trip; the rule is not determined only by where a fish was caught.
Federal tuna limits apply per 24-hour period at sea and never authorize more than one daily bag per calendar day. Multi-day possession needs separate review.

South of Point Conception (34°27′ N), tuna processed aboard must use the six-piece arrangement required by §27.65, keep all skin attached, and be individually bagged with its species labeled. That specific six-piece rule does not apply to processing north of the line.

rod.note: This profile is for recreational rod-and-reel fishing from a boat. Read the species-specific hook, line, retention and on-board restrictions below.

bluefin.name: Pacific bluefin tuna
bluefin.season: Year-round in the reviewed 2026 rules. Offshore U.S. waters off this part of California.
bluefin.bag: 2 per person daily and in possession on a day trip, in addition to the general 20-finfish limit.
bluefin.size: No minimum size in these recreational rules.
details: The bluefin possession limit applies regardless of where fish were taken. This card does not cover Mexico or Atlantic bluefin.
General ocean hook-and-line rules apply; fish already aboard can impose stricter rod and hook limits.
If processing tuna aboard south of Point Conception, follow the tuna-specific fillet, skin and bag-label requirements in §27.65. Check special rules before any multi-day trip.
Federal limits apply per 24-hour period at sea and never authorize more than one daily bag per calendar day. Commercial Pacific bluefin quotas and Atlantic tuna alerts are different fisheries.

rod.note: This profile is for recreational rod-and-reel fishing from a boat. Read the species-specific hook, line, retention and on-board restrictions below.

dungeness.name: Dungeness crab
dungeness.season: Open from Nov 7, 2026 (south of the Mendocino/Sonoma county line). Crab traps are prohibited until at least Jan 1, 2027; hoop nets and crab snares are permitted.

windows.restriction: Open from Nov 7, 2026. Crab traps are prohibited until at least Jan 1, 2027; hoop nets and crab snares are permitted.

dungeness.bag: When open: 10 per person daily; 10 in possession on a private boat.
dungeness.size: 5¾ in shell width, measured across the body just in front of the side spines, excluding those spines. Carry a crab gauge.
details: Season opening and trap permission are separate. CDFW (Nov 7, 2026): crab traps may not be set or fished in ocean waters, and a Fleet Advisory is in effect; the Oct 30 risk assessment prohibits traps until at least Jan 1, 2027. Check CDFW whale-safe and health notices.
A crab-trap validation is required to use traps. Maximum 10 deployed traps per person; required escape rings, destruct device, GO ID and buoy markings apply.
Hoop nets and snares have separate gear rules. A trap restriction does not itself close those methods, but the season and health closures still apply.
Check the current 2026 hoop-net marking rules and all gear details in §29.80 before setting gear.
Crab traps may not be deployed during the seven days before the Dungeness season opens. Service deployed traps at intervals no greater than nine days, weather conditions permitting (§29.80(c)).
Crab loop traps or snares may have no more than six loops. Hoop nets must be raised and inspected at least every two hours (§29.80).

North of Point Arguello, each hoop net must have the required surface buoy marked with the operator’s GO ID; the main buoy may not exceed 6 in in diameter or 14 in in length. An optional orange marker marked H and its connecting line have additional marking specifications; check §29.80(b) before rigging.

trap.note: Trap permission is checked separately from the Dungeness season and health closures. Confirm the current recreational trap declaration, validation, marking and tending rules before setting.

hoop.note: A hoop net is a different gear category from a crab trap. Follow the current hoop-net construction, attendance and deployment rules; season and health closures still apply.

snare.note: Use the current snare definition and gear limits. A trap restriction does not by itself establish permission to take Dungeness; the season and health checks also apply.
